chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from a number of our companions, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Husayn ibn Kharjah, from Maysar ibn Abdul Aziz, who said:
Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Do not have dealings with those who have deformities, for they are the most unjust of things.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the people with whom dealings are abhorred according to al-Kafi?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises against engaging in transactions or close social mingling with those suffering from chronic ailments or physical deformities, characterizing them as 'the most unjust' (azlam). While 'injustice' here may refer to their tendency to be demanding or quick to feel wronged due to their condition, Shia scholars also note this as a practical guideline for maintaining social harmony and avoiding potential friction in dealings.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from a number of our companions, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Husayn Bin Kharjat, from Maysar Bin Abdul Aziz who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Do not have dealings with the ones with deformities, for they are the most unjust ones’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bandar has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu ‘Abd Alfah, from his father from Fadf al- Nawfafiy from ibn abu Yahya al-Raziy who has said the fofiowing:
“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘You must not intermingle or form contract with anyone except those who are established in goodness.’”
